cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: Basically Finished
cards.instruction: Describe incomplete, late, or improvised work as a thoughtful version of completion.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've approved your cupboard as finished. The loose shelves preserve your freedom to choose heights.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Can you fit the supports? They fall down.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Adjustment is approved. This is the completed kit edition; you may arrange it around your tins.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I paid for installation. Can you use this drill and finish it?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: A demonstration is authorized. I'll fasten one shelf at your height: a finished sample. You may admire the remaining possibilities without rushing them.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 approves incomplete work as finished, A3 grants adjustment under a kit label, and A5 authorizes one demonstration as a finished sample.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 missing supports causes A3 kit reinterpretation; B4 drill and paid scope cause A5 one actual shelf installed under another completion label.

relationship.evidence: B2 reports functional failure and B4 seeks the paid work with a tool, giving A credible pressure rather than passive disappointment.

heightening.evidence: B4 insistence obtains a small action, which A5 immediately redescribes as sufficient thoughtful completion.

specificity.evidence: A1 loose shelves and B2 falling supports make incompleteness explicit; B4 states the installation duty.
